Local routing is an advanced feature. Please make sure you understand how it works before enabling.

We recommend consulting the relevant documentation or your provider for proper configuration.

failover.title: Enable Failover

Failover is an advanced feature. Please make sure you understand how it works before enabling.

We recommend configuring provider priorities in the failover queue first.

unifyCodexHistory.title: Unified Codex session history
unifyCodexHistory.message:
When enabled, the Codex CLI resume list shows official subscription and third-party sessions together (the Codex desktop app can show all sessions since a recent update and is unaffected). Note: resuming an old session across providers may fail because the other backend cannot decrypt its encrypted_content reasoning.

You can also migrate your existing official session history into the shared list (backed up to ~/.aicli-client/backups first; you can restore it when turning this off).
unifyCodexHistory.migrateExisting: Also migrate existing official session history

unifyCodexHistoryOff.title: Turn off unified session history
unifyCodexHistoryOff.message: When turned off, the Codex CLI goes back to separate session lists for the official subscription and third-party providers (the desktop app still shows all sessions). Sessions created while this was on can't be told apart, so they stay in the third-party history and the CLI won't show them under the official subscription.
unifyCodexHistoryOff.restoreBackup: Restore the official sessions migrated at enable time back to the official history (exact restore from backup)

usage.title: Configure Usage Query
usage.message:
Usage query requires a custom script or API parameters. Please make sure you have obtained the necessary information from your provider.

If unsure how to configure, please consult your provider's documentation first.

autoSync.title: Enable Auto Sync
autoSync.message:
When auto sync is enabled, every database change will be automatically uploaded to the WebDAV server.

This may result in significant network traffic. Please ensure your network and WebDAV service can handle frequent data transfers.

rectifier.description: Automatically fix API request compatibility issues
rectifier.thinkingSignatureDescription: When an Anthropic-type provider returns thinking signature incompatibility or illegal request errors, automatically removes incompatible thinking-related blocks and retries once with the same provider
rectifier.thinkingBudgetDescription: When an Anthropic-type provider returns budget_tokens constraint errors (such as at least 1024), automatically normalizes thinking to enabled, sets thinking budget to 32000, and raises max_tokens to 64000 if needed, then retries once

settings.skipClaudeOnboardingDescription: On first launch, Claude Code runs an onboarding flow that asks you to pick a theme and sign in to an Anthropic account. If you use a third-party provider you don't need that sign-in, so turning this on skips straight past it. It works by writing hasCompletedOnboarding: true to ~/.claude.json; turning it off removes that field, and the onboarding appears again on the next launch.
settings.preserveCodexOfficialAuthOnSwitch: Keep official login for direct switches
settings.preserveCodexOfficialAuthOnSwitchDescrip: Controls third-party switches when local routing is off. Takeover routing always preserves the Codex official login.
settings.unifyCodexSessionHistoryDescription: Affects the Codex CLI only: its resume list shows only the current provider's sessions. When enabled, the official subscription runs under the shared "custom" provider id so official and third-party sessions appear in one list. The Codex desktop app can show all sessions since a recent update, so desktop-only users don't need this. You can optionally migrate existing official sessions in (backed up first) and restore them from backup when turning it off. Note: resuming an old session across providers may fail because its encrypted_content reasoning can only be decrypted by the backend that created it.
settings.codexStackClassicSubagentsDescription: Must be on when the main agent and a sub-agent use different providers, or the sub-agent cannot receive its task.
settings.codexStackClassicSubagentsForcedV2: Codex config.toml turns on [features] multi_agent_v2, which takes precedence over this setting, so it has no effect.
settings.codexSessionCompressionDescription: When on, Codex compresses session files that haven't changed for 7 days in the background each time it starts, which saves a lot of disk space. Codex decompresses a session automatically when you continue it. AICLI Client still lists and counts compressed sessions; the list just doesn't show a preview of their last reply. This is a Codex feature still under development: Codex shows a notice on every start while it's on. Requires a recent Codex version and takes effect after restarting Codex. Turning it off stops compressing; sessions already compressed stay as they are.

usage.speedHelp: Output tokens per second, from the first token to the end. Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count; for models that hide their reasoning it's an approximation. A value with ≈ is estimated from session-log timestamps when routing is off: the wait for the first token is included, so the number reads low. Only requests with at least 200 output tokens are estimated.
usage.speedSumHelp: Total output tokens divided by total generation time, not an average of per-request speeds, so short requests don't skew it. Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count. A value with ≈ is estimated from session logs (it includes the wait for the first token, and only requests with at least 200 output tokens count) and is shown only when the row has no routed data.
usage.firstTokenHelp: Time from the routing service receiving the request to the upstream starting its output. A value with ≈ is derived from session-log timestamps when routing is off: it starts from when the previous log line was written, so it includes the client's own request preparation and reads high. Claude Code only yields one when the reply starts with thinking; Codex only with newer logs, and not when the reply opens with a tool call.
usage.firstTokenSumHelp: Time from the routing service receiving a request to the upstream starting its output. The row shows the median across its requests, so an occasional slow request (queueing, cold start) doesn't pull it up. Only successful streaming requests through the routing service count; requests older than 30 days, already folded into daily rollups, don't. A value with ≈ is derived from session logs (it reads high, and only some requests yield one) and is shown only when the row has no routed data.
